summary: A tired batch. The Commons and Uncommons are mostly fine object habits (accordion clearing its throat, drum at 7am on Saturday, double bass needing a bus seat, recorder practised in the kitchen, theremin frightening the cat, sousaphone spun by the wind), and a few Epics land (cajon bouncing sausages, bagpipes lining up sheep, trumpet spinning the tombola, guitar pick in the singer's hair). The problems are structural: (1) about 30 Rares are the template 'plays so X that everyone nearby does Y', a crowd reaction instead of a troublesome power; (2) Epics are 'played at an event so X that the crowd Y' scenes; (3) Legendaries are mostly 'has done X so many times / for fifty years / never once' or a quiet success, and 54 of 56 Legendary names are 'The X That Y'; (4) an echo-across-the-hills frame repeats (djembe, bagpipes, trumpet, church bell, w10 guitar amp) and a parade frame repeats (conga, sousaphone, shaker, euphonium); (5) copies of approved or other-batch content: banana bunch Rare = Pilot 02 banana Rare, singing bowl and sitar Uncommons = Pilot 02 tuning fork, music box = w08 x_music_box and w16 x_music_box_toy, metronome Uncommon = w10 drum machine, banana split Epic = w22 milkshake. Sensitive: the church bell is meant to be a village tower bell, but its Uncommon (Sunday morning) and Epic (wedding peal) imply church. Mechanics: move names are mostly truthful (poison=stink, burn=heat, stun=startle); fixes are Ultimates that repeat Epic names (electric bass, toy piano, recorder, cymbal, handbell, wind chime) and a recorder 'spit valve', which recorders do not have. Signatures are almost all 'X Startle' (pattern, low). All replacements were checked by script: lore 60-160 characters, ASCII, names within limits and unique across all content/curated/*.json and the Pilot 01 names proposal.

patterns.pattern: Rare template 'plays so X that everyone nearby does Y': a crowd reaction instead of a troublesome power (about 30 of 56 Rares).
patterns.suggestion: Give each Rare a power that causes trouble (sucks napkins off tables, sours the milk, pops soap bubbles, snaps shut on sandwiches). Replacements are given per object.

patterns.pattern: Legendary names: 54 of 56 are 'The X That/Of Y' (only accordion and drum differ).
patterns.suggestion: Replacement names for every Legendary are given, mixing epithets ('Name the Y', 'Name, the Y'), titles (Baron, Signor, Professor, Countess) and puns (Crashendo, Buzzalot, Plinkerton).

patterns.pattern: Legendary formula 'has done X so many times / for N years / never once / never missed' or a quiet success with no punchline.
patterns.suggestion: Each is replaced with a concrete outrageous feat and a punchline.

patterns.pattern: Echo and parade frames: 'heard across the valley / the next village came out' (djembe, bagpipes, trumpet, church bell; w10 guitar amp) and 'led the parade / carnival' (conga, sousaphone, shaker, euphonium; w05 gondola).
patterns.suggestion: Church bell keeps its seven villages and conga keeps its endless parade; the others are changed.

patterns.pattern: Copies of approved or other-batch lines: banana bunch R = Pilot 02 banana R; singing bowl U and sitar U = Pilot 02 tuning fork C; music box U/E/L = w08 x_music_box R/E and w16 x_music_box_toy L; metronome U = w10 drum machine R; banana split E = w22 milkshake E; plantain chips U = w21 samosa U; euphonium L = w05 gondola E.
patterns.suggestion: Replacements given; none reuses the other object's image.

patterns.pattern: One trait scaled over three rarities: conga (conga line U/E/L), rain stick (fake rain U/R/E), banana bunch (ripening U/R/E), bell (dinner call R/E), sitar (lost time R/E/L), bugle (wake-up E/L), timpani/cymbal (ended every song).
patterns.suggestion: Five premises per object; replacements given for the repeated rarities.

patterns.pattern: Epic names that do not match their lore (sheet music 'Grade Exam Panic', djembe 'Village Gathering', guitar 'Bedroom Rock Star' on a campfire line, harmonica 'Porch Step Blues' on a station platform) and name-lore mismatches lower down (music stand U, sheet music U, harp U, euphonium R).
patterns.suggestion: Names re-paired to the lore; write names after the lore.

patterns.pattern: Ultimates that repeat the Epic name (electric bass, toy piano, recorder, cymbal, handbell, wind chime, sousaphone; partly bagpipes, bugle, shaker, trumpet).
patterns.suggestion: Effect-neutral replacements given where variants differ.

patterns.pattern: Signature monotony: 51 of 56 signatures are '<Sound> Startle' (truthful for the stun signature, but identical in shape across the batch).
patterns.suggestion: Vary with 'Flash', 'Jolt', 'Blare', 'Clang' or a sound alone ('Bop Bop', 'Tock').

patterns.pattern: Sensitive: x_church_bell is written as a village tower bell per the tracker, but 'early on a Sunday morning' and a wedding peal imply church services.
patterns.suggestion: Saturday wake-up and fete-day replacements given.

patterns.pattern: Banana objects (bunch, peel, split, plantain chips) sit in this batch by visual class; their lore is written for the real food, which is right.
patterns.suggestion: No change needed beyond the per-object fixes.
